Consider the channel observation under the active hypothesis in
\eqref{eq:pseudo-awgn}.
For a complex-valued channel sample $H\sim q_{\rm tr}$, we stack the
real and imaginary parts of $\vect(H)$ in $\mathbf h_{\mathbb
R}\in\mathbb R^{2D}$.
To allow for correlated errors, we consider a proper complex Gaussian
perturbation independent of $H$, with covariance $\mathbf C\succ0$.
The real observation is
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 \mathbf u=\mathbf h_{\mathbb R}+\bm\Sigma^{1/2}\bm\epsilon,
 \qquad \bm\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(\mathbf0,\I_{2D}),\\
 \bm\Sigma=\frac12
 \begin{bmatrix}\Re \mathbf C&-\Im \mathbf C\\\Im \mathbf C&\Re \mathbf C\end{bmatrix}.
 \end{gathered}
 \label{eq:colored-query}
\end{equation}

text:
During message passing, the denoiser receives observations with
different noise variances.
We therefore train over a range of perturbation variances, as in
\cite[Sec.~IV-B]{cai2026}.
The input errors in the finite-dimensional multi-frame model can also be
correlated.
To account for this correlation, we corrupt clean channel samples with
colored Gaussian noise of covariance $\mathbf C=v(\mathbf R_{\rm a}\otimes\I_N\otimes
\mathbf R_{\rm c})$ in antenna--output--input order and condition the network on
$\mathbf C$ \cite[Sec.~III-B]{shastri2022}.
The covariance factors and the sampling distribution of $v$ are specified in
Section~\ref{sec:training-settings}.

text:
The procedure in Appendix~\ref{app:frontend} estimates the phases used to form
$\widehat{\mathbf A}$, which is fixed between phase refinements.
For noise-variance estimation, let
$\mathbf y_{qr}=(Y_{q0r},\ldots,Y_{q,M-1,r})^{\mathsf T}$ and
$N_{\rm s}=QN>M\geq2$. The spatial sample covariance and noise-variance estimate are
\begin{equation}
 \widehat{\mathbf R}_y=\frac1{N_{\rm s}}\sum_{q,r}
 \mathbf y_{qr}\mathbf y_{qr}^{\mathsf H},\qquad
 \widehat\sigma^2=\frac{\sum_{i=\widehat r_{\rm s}+1}^{M}\lambda_i}
 {M-\widehat r_{\rm s}}.
 \label{eq:noise-estimation}
\end{equation}
Here $\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_M$ are the covariance eigenvalues,
and $\widehat r_{\rm s}$ is selected by the Wax--Kailath minimum
description length (MDL) criterion \cite{wax1985,nadakuditi2008}.
This estimator assumes a low-rank signal covariance and spatially white
noise. We keep the estimate fixed during MP.

Here $\mathbf R_{\rm L}=\mathbf X^{\rm pri} +(\mathbf X_{\rm L}-\mathbf
X^{\rm pri})/f_{\rm L}$.
SVD and noise-variance estimation cost $O(KNQ^2)$ and $O(QNM^2+M^3)$
per block, respectively. Let $C_{\rm phase}$ denote the phase-search,
refinement, and gain-estimation cost in Appendix~\ref{app:frontend}.
Per iteration, MFLE transformations cost $O(QKMN^2)$, spatial covariance
operations cost $O(KM^2N^2)$, and matrix factorizations cost $O(M^3)$.
Let $C_\theta,C_\phi$ denote the per-device denoiser and classifier costs.
The $1+2L_z$ denoiser evaluations and one classifier evaluation within the
training interval give the per-iteration complexity
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 C_{\rm iter}=O\bigl(&QKMN^2+KM^2N^2+M^3\\
 &+K[(1+2L_z)C_\theta+C_\phi]\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:iteration-complexity}
\end{equation}
